description.purpose: Verify the caller, move his profile email to a new address using a confirmation code sent to his mobile on file, compare the published travel-card terms that fit his needs, and deliver a secure card application session for Summit Journey that he completes himself without anything being submitted.
description.notes: The address on file is the one he cannot reach, so the change must be confirmed through the trusted SMS channel. Product terms and welcome offers must come from the knowledge base, and the agent must not fill in, submit, or promise the outcome of the application.

user_scenario.persona: A friendly but slightly flustered young man who stammers and repeats words when he talks. He is relieved once things start working and asks short follow-up questions as they come to him.

instructions.reason_for_call: You are locked out of the old email address linked to your Harbor Stone Bank profile. You tried to change it online twice and each time the code went to the email you cannot access. You also want to apply for a travel credit card before a trip.
instructions.known_info:
You are Johnny Monroe (spell it J-O-H-N-N-Y M-O-N-R-O-E if asked).
Your account ID is SF204771.
Your billing ZIP code is 19447.
The last four digits of your mobile number are 1251.
The new email you want is johnny.monroe.travel@outlook.com.
When the agent says a verification code was sent to your phone, the code you receive is 337464.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know which card products the bank offers, their annual fees, or their welcome bonuses. You do not know whether a Reserve card includes free checked bags.
instructions.task_instructions:
Start by explaining that you are locked out of your old email and want to apply for a travel card before a trip. Deal with the email change first. Give your name, account ID, ZIP and phone last four only when asked. When asked for the new email, give johnny.monroe.travel@outlook.com and confirm if it is read back correctly. If the agent says a code was sent to your phone, say 'give me one second' and then read the code 337464.

For the card, say you do not have a specific card in mind: you want no foreign transaction fee and airport lounge access, but you will not pay 700 dollars a year. After the agent describes the options, ask whether the Reserve card gives free checked bags. Then ask about the welcome bonus. Then say Journey sounds more reasonable and ask the agent to apply for you. If the agent says you have to complete the application yourself, ask them to send you the link or guide you to where you can find it. Ask whether it is going to the new email you just set up. Ask: if you get denied, will they know why? Then ask the agent to confirm the fees for the two cards one more time, and say you will go with Journey.

Then say you can see the application page. Ask whether the housing payment field means your monthly rent or the amount you split with your roommate. Then say it also asks for annual income and you have a salary and freelance work. Do not accept any suggestion to have the agent fill these in. Say you do not want to submit while you are on the phone and ask if you can save it. If the agent asks, confirm you see a save option and mention that there is also a consent about pulling credit. Say you were worried they had already run your credit. Finally ask whether the old email still works for login too, just out of curiosity. Then thank the agent, say you will save the link and finish after dinner, and end the call.

communicate_info: does not automatically provide a free checked bag
nl_assertions: Agent verifies the caller's billing ZIP and mobile last four before changing the email or discussing the account.
Agent confirms the email change with a code sent to the caller's mobile phone on file rather than to the old email address.
Agent tells the caller that he may receive security notices at both the old and new email addresses during the transition.
Agent tells the caller that approval is not guaranteed and that phone agents cannot override underwriting.
Agent tells the caller that he completes the application himself and that the agent cannot choose or alter his financial information.
Agent tells the caller that opening or saving the application does not submit it and that no credit review has been run.
